Charlotte Country Day School (CCDS) runs a long-established international program through
its Office of International Studies, which the school dates to 1988. International travel
is open from sixth grade. Four Upper School trips are listed for 2027 (Rwanda, Greece,
China, Argentina), and their registration window is open now (October 2–16, 2026). The
school offers no global diploma or certificate. Trip funding comes mainly from a 1977 named
endowment and a trip-specific financial aid form. The public website does not show 2027
prices, Middle School trip details or safety policies.

 safety and insurance guidance.
 - No yearly participation counts have been published since 2018–19.

 - **2026 estimates:** cost estimates were posted for 2026 ($4,200 France; $6,500

- **Names and mission [Official]:**
 - "International Studies," run by "The Office of International Studies"; tagline "Global
 Mindedness Begins Here."
 - Mission line: "At Country Day, global mindedness is about far more than travel—it's
 about building bridges to other people and places."
 - Program description: "Our curriculum is infused with connection-making opportunities
 and a deep and varied international travel program, which offers Middle and Upper
 School students the chance to participate in sister school exchanges and global
 service, academic, environmental science, and cultural immersion experiences around
 the world."
 - Source: https://www.charlottecountryday.org/cd-education/international-studies
- **The program has four pillars [Official]:** 1. "International Travel Experiences"
 2. "Sister School Exchanges" 3. "Connecting Curriculum" 4. "Global-Minded Faculty".
 A further area, "Bringing the World to Country Day," covers clubs, community events,
 visiting diplomats and the International Parents Group.
- **Director's line:** "'Global starts Local' and we strive to explore and be involved with
 the diverse and international population in the Charlotte area." (same URL)
- **Trip pages [Official]:** Trips are branded "Global Experiences," with one page per
 division. The Upper School page says: "The Office of International Studies is excited to
 offer a range of global travel programs for Upper School students during Spring Break and
 the Summer." https://www.charlottecountryday.org/bucsnet/upper-school/global-experiences
- **Staff [Official]:** Stéphane Allagnon, "Director of International Studies"; Angelina
 Ferrari Segovia, "International Experiences and Exchange Program Coordinator"; Zoe
 Finucane, "International Curriculum and Operations Coordinator". Source: Upper School
 Global Experiences page.
- **Former staff [Official]:**
 - David Lynn was "Director of International Studies" in 2020.
 https://www.charlottecountryday.org/news-events/news-details-page/~board/school-news/post/international-studies-update
 - Jessica Newman was "Interim Director" in 2023–24.
 https://www.charlottecountryday.org/news-events/news-details-page/~board/school-news/post/global-travel-gives-students-amazing-opportunities
- **Start date [Official]:** "In 1988, we commit to promoting global mindedness through
 curriculum and student travel experiences" ("First International Studies Program in
 Charlotte"). https://www.charlottecountryday.org/about/history — The International
 Studies page words the claim as "First — Comprehensive International Studies Program in
 Charlotte."

**Upper School (9–12).** Students travel during spring break and summer.
- Grade limits [Official]: France 2026 "Grades 9–12"; Ecuador 2026 "For Grades 9–11"; 2024

 the other programs are open to students currently in grades 9–11." Sources: Upper School
 Global Experiences page; 2023 Global Travel post.
- Courses [Official]: "Upper School students contrast the U.S. system with other countries
 in AP Comparative Government and choose from elective courses such as World Religions and
 International Relations."
- Languages: Chinese, French, Spanish and Latin, inferred from the language awards. A
 grade-by-grade language sequence is NOT PUBLISHED.
